key_points: Teams should identify business problems and redesign target processes before building automation.
Agents must have clear, bounded responsibilities and use structured output for reliability.
Deterministic steps should handle predictable logic while agents manage genuine judgment.
Human review is essential for high-stakes cases, and evaluation must be continuous.
Identity management should match the automation's operational context, using service or user authentication.
items.summary: The article outlines strategies for creating production-grade agentic automations using Amazon Quick Automate. The author emphasizes that process quality determines agent quality, urging teams to identify business problems before designing automation. Key recommendations include defining clear success metrics and redesigning workflows to eliminate unnecessary manual steps. The text advises designing agents with bounded responsibilities and combining them with deterministic steps for predictable execution. Human-in-the-loop mechanisms are recommended for high-stakes decisions, while evaluation and observability must be treated as ongoing disciplines. Finally, the author suggests managing identity and access thoughtfully based on whether the automation runs unattended or on a user's behalf.

key_points: NVIDIA reduced repeated login events by 55% by implementing a central identity gateway pattern.
The pattern separates session ownership from request enforcement to ensure consistent logout and token refresh.
Regional gateways validate sessions against a shared store instead of managing their own login flows.
AI assistants can inherit user identity context without requiring separate credentials for each backend tool.
Teams should migrate incrementally by defining a central contract and replacing local validation with a central call.
items.summary: The article describes a central identity gateway pattern for propagating user identity across federated Kubernetes and AI platforms. NVIDIA reported that this approach reduced repeated login events by 55% across internal developer platforms spanning AWS and OCI clusters. The pattern separates session ownership from request enforcement to solve problems like inconsistent logout and uncoordinated token refresh. A central gateway manages login, session state, and lifecycle, while regional gateways validate sessions against a shared store. This design allows AI assistants to act with delegated user identity without needing separate credentials for every tool. The authors note that distributed session state creates architectural debt, leading to duplicated logic and fragmented user context. Implementing this pattern requires defining a central contract for session creation and validation claims. Teams should migrate incrementally, starting with one gateway before expanding to others. The architecture relies on standard OIDC, a shared session store like Redis, and stateless regional gateways. Centralizing identity also reduces load on upstream identity providers by coordinating refreshes and policy evaluations in one place. Finally, the article suggests using open-source projects like OAuth2 Proxy and Istio to build similar gateway architectures.
items.title: NVIDIA reduces logins by 55% using a central identity gateway pattern

items.summary: The authors report that embedding Amazon QuickSight visuals into React applications requires a dedicated identity layer to manage per-user authentication and data access. This post details a serverless architecture using Amazon Cognito, AWS Lambda, and API Gateway to generate scoped embed URLs for registered users. The solution automatically provisions new users in QuickSight with READER roles upon their first login. Access control operates at multiple levels, including API Gateway validation, Lambda-based user registration, and dashboard sharing permissions. The authors explain that the QuickSight account must register the application's CloudFront domain in its embedding allowlist to prevent cross-origin rendering errors. Users can interact with embedded visuals through custom filters exposed via the QuickSight Embedding SDK. The implementation involves deploying a CloudFormation stack, configuring a React front end, and manually sharing dashboards with authenticated users. By the end of the guide, developers can render individual QuickSight visuals within their applications while maintaining strict role-based access control.
